- Overestimate prices when sentiment is consistently high (0.80+), especially in early forecast periods.  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (0.00–0.27) or shows strong negative momentum.  
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes in history; model tends to overreact and then correct too late.  
- Mean-reversion bias: model often holds prices too high in trending upward periods, especially when sentiment is mixed or neutral.  
- Forecast horizon 30d: model tends to over-predict early in the period when sentiment is bullish, then under-predict later when sentiment turns neutral or bearish.  
- When sentiment drops below 0.50, model should reduce forecast slope and avoid aggressive upward revisions.  
- If last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model should not assume continuation of upward trend unless sentiment rebounds sharply.
